Pension Plans

Build a steady stream of income for your golden years.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between NPS and traditional pension plans?

NPS is market-linked with equity/debt allocation choices, offers tax benefits under 80CCD, and allows 60% lump sum withdrawal at 60. Traditional plans (like LIC Jeevan Shanti) offer guaranteed returns and fixed annuity rates.

When should I start investing in a pension plan?

Ideally in your 30s. The power of compounding works best over 25-30 years. Starting early means lower monthly contributions for the same retirement corpus. It's never too late to start, though.

Are pension plan returns taxable?

Annuity payouts are taxable as per your income tax slab. However, NPS allows 60% tax-free withdrawal at 60, and 40% must be used to buy annuity (taxable). Traditional plans have different tax treatment for commutation vs pension.
